findings.claim: On any day with a date override, a slot inside the override window returns true at `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` before `busy.every(...)` runs. Existing bookings and calendar busy times are ignored, which allows double bookings on the fixed-host and round-robin host paths.
findings.evidence: All three seats reason the same early return (lines 133-135); before the patch the busy check always ran. superpowers reports repro.mjs case 3 printing true (predicate level only; the orchestrator did not observe this). Proposed red tests: mattpocock snippet 1 in override-ignores-busy.test-snippet.ts (booking at 09:30Z inside the IST override); open-code-review adds a booking for user 101 at plus2 08:30-09:29:59Z and expects 08:30Z absent. Neither has been run.

verifier.reason: In checkIfIsAvailable, any slot on a date-override day that is not rejected at slots.ts:105-131 returns true at slots.ts:133-135, so the `busy.every(...)` check at slots.ts:153 never runs. The fixed-host path (slots.ts:488-493) and the round-robin path (slots.ts:513-518) both spread each user's availability, which includes `dateOverrides` and `busy`, so existing bookings and calendar busy times are ignored on those days.

findings.claim: The working-hours check uses `workingHours.find(day matches && slot outside wh)`, which means 'outside ANY range' instead of 'inside SOME range'. Any day with more than one working-hours entry loses valid slots. This covers split hours such as 09-12 plus 13-17, and hours that getWorkingHours splits at UTC midnight. The branch now runs for every fixed host, including all personal event types.
findings.evidence: open-code-review and superpowers cite packages/lib/availability.ts getWorkingHours splitting America/Los_Angeles 9-17 into [1-5] 1020-1439 plus [2-6] 0-60. The seats disagree on magnitude: open-code-review says the last hour of Mon-Thu is lost, superpowers says all Tue-Fri slots are lost. mattpocock notes `isFixed: !schedulingType` (line 369) widens the reach. superpowers reports repro.mjs cases 1 and 2 printing true (seat-reported). Proposed red test (open-code-review): a single user with 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 UTC on all days expects slots and gets none. Not run.
findings.reason: Accepted. Severity normalised to Critical (2 of 3 seats; it removes availability for common schedules on every event type). Needs the split-hours getSchedule test made red first.

verifier.reason: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:138-151, `workingHours.find` rejects a slot as soon as any entry for that weekday has the slot outside its range. With 09-12 plus 13-17, a 10:00 slot falls outside 13-17 and a 14:00 slot falls outside 9-12, so every slot is dropped. getWorkingHours (packages/lib/availability.ts:93-110) also splits a schedule at UTC midnight into two entries. The check runs for every fixed host (lines 484-493), and isFixed is true for every non-team event type (line 369).

findings.claim: In the working-hours check, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`. A slot that runs past the end of working hours is never rejected.
findings.evidence: All four seats identify the copy-paste at line 142. ponytail example: hours 9:00-17:00, 60-min event, 30-min interval; the 16:30 slot ending 17:30 passes. ponytail says this is reachable for collective events where another fixed host's override replaces the combined working hours. Reasoned; no seat ran a test.
findings.reason: Accepted. Red test still to be written: a slot whose end exceeds working hours must be absent. Fix by using slotEndTime.

verifier.reason: At packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142, the patch sets `end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, which is the same value as `start` on line 141. `slotEndTime` from line 99 is never used, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` test on line 143 cannot reject a slot that starts inside working hours but runs past their end.

findings.claim: An override is matched to slots by the UTC calendar date of its shifted start (`format("YYYY MM DD")`), not by the organizer's local date. An override near local midnight therefore lands on the adjacent UTC date, and every slot on that date outside the window is rejected. Overrides east of UTC wipe the previous day, and those west of UTC wipe the next day. In-override slots on the other UTC date skip the override. Separately, `dayjs(date.start)...format()` uses the server's local zone while `slotStartTime` is UTC, so results depend on the server TZ.
findings.evidence: Seat examples: IST unavailable override 00:00 D becomes D-1 18:30Z (mattpocock); Australia/Sydney Jan 10 09:00-12:00 local (open-code-review); UTC-7 18:00-20:00 Nov 17 (superpowers). superpowers reports repro.mjs case 4 printing true (seat-reported). Proposed red test: mattpocock snippet 2 (unavailable override on plus3, expects all 8 plus2 slots). Not run.
findings.reason: Accepted. Severity normalised to Important (open-code-review and superpowers say Important; mattpocock says Critical). Needs snippet 2 shown red first.

verifier.reason: At slots.ts:107-111, `date.start` is the organizer's wall-clock time stored as UTC (getUserAvailability.ts:218-222). Shifting it by the offset gives a UTC instant, and only its date is compared with `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`, so an override near local midnight is applied to the adjacent UTC date and rejects that date's out-of-window slots at lines 117-124. `dayjs(date.start)` is not `.utc()` and @calcom/dayjs sets no default zone, so the formatted date also depends on the server's time zone.

findings.claim: The override containment check only tests `slotEndTime <= start` and `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)`. Slots that partially overlap the override are accepted: one that starts inside and ends after it, one that starts before and ends inside it, and one that starts exactly at the override end. In round-robin this is the only per-host gate, so a host can be assigned a slot past their override.
findings.evidence: mattpocock (lines 117-125), open-code-review (line 123; example: host B override 09:00-12:00 assigned 11:30-12:30), superpowers (line 124). Reasoned.
findings.reason: Accepted. Severity normalised to Important (2 of 3; superpowers rated Minor). Red test to write: a slot straddling the override end must be absent.

verifier.reason: The new override check in slots.ts:117-125 rejects a slot only if slotEnd <= override start or slotStart is after override end, so slots that partly overlap the override (or start exactly at its end) fall through to `dateOverrideExist` and return true at slots.ts:133-135, which also skips the busy check. One caveat: in round-robin, buildSlots (packages/lib/slots.ts:90) already leaves a host's ID off a slot that does not fit that host's override, so this is not the only per-host gate there. The bug still lets fixed/collective hosts be booked past their override when another host's hours produce the slot.

findings.claim: `dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares object identity and is always false. The intended start==end 'unavailable all day' branch is dead code, and a slot starting exactly at that instant falls through.
findings.evidence: All four seats agree on identity comparison. superpowers notes getSlots masks it in practice.
findings.reason: Accepted. Delete the branch or use `.isSame(...)`. Severity normalised to Minor (ponytail rated Important).

verifier.reason: At packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 the patch compares two separately built Dayjs objects with `===`, which checks object identity, so the condition is always false and the start==end ('unavailable all day') branch never runs. A slot starting exactly at that instant is not caught by isBefore/isSame at :118-119 (its end is after the instant) or by isAfter at :123 (its start equals the instant), so it falls through to `dateOverrideExist` → return true at :133-134 and is reported available.

findings.claim: The `activeOverrides` day filter still selects the invitee day by treating the organizer wall-clock value (stored as if UTC) as a real instant. The offset correction is only half applied, so the shifted override can land on the wrong invitee day.

Reasoned.

verifier.reason: packages/lib/slots.ts:206-208 still picks overrides with `dayjs.utc(override.start)`, but getUserAvailability.ts:218-221 stores the organizer's wall-clock time as if it were UTC. The offset is applied only to the hours and minutes (slots.ts:211-224), so an IST override for 02:00–05:00 on D is placed on the UTC invitee's day D at 20:30–23:30 instead of D-1, where it really starts.

findings.claim: `startTime`/`endTime` are computed as `hour()*60+minute()` with no day carry. When the shifted override crosses the invitee's midnight, `endTime < startTime` and buildSlots skips the range (`if (start >= end) continue`). Working hours for that day were already removed, so the day has zero slots. This regression is new.
findings.evidence: Seat examples: IST 14:00-18:00 viewed from +12:00 gives 20:30-00:30 (mattpocock); New_York 09:00-17:00 viewed from Asia/Kolkata gives 1110 to 150 (open-code-review); +6 05:00-08:00 viewed from UTC gives 23:00 to 02:00 (superpowers). Reasoned.

verifier.reason: At packages/lib/slots.ts:218-223 the patch shifts each override by the gap between the invitee's and organizer's UTC offsets, then keeps only `hour()*60+minute()`, so the day carry is lost. For New York 09:00-17:00 viewed from Kolkata this gives startTime 1110 and endTime 150. buildSlots then drops the range at slots.ts:68 (`if (start >= end) continue`), and the user's working hours for that day were already removed at slots.ts:228-243, so the day has no slots.

findings.claim: `TimeRange.timeZone` is optional. When it is undefined, `.tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the process timezone, so results depend on the host machine.

verifier.reason: The patch makes `timeZone` optional at packages/types/schedule.d.ts:248, and packages/lib/slots.ts:212 calls `.tz(override.timeZone)` without a guard. With no default set in dayjs, an undefined value resolves to the host machine's timezone. Today nothing reaches that path: the only caller that passes overrides (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:410-414) sets `timeZone` from getUserAvailability (packages/core/getUserAvailability.ts:201), which falls back to the non-null `User.timeZone` (schema.prisma:161), and the TeamAvailabilityTimes callers pass no dateOverrides.

findings.claim: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` round-trips through non-ISO `Date#toString()` output. That parsing is engine-dependent and drops milliseconds; `dayjs(override.start)` is sufficient.

verifier.reason: packages/lib/slots.ts:212-213 (added by the patch) call `dayjs(override.start.toString())`. `Date#toString()` produces a non-ISO string with no milliseconds, so dayjs hands it to `new Date(string)`, which is engine-dependent. Using `dayjs(override.start)` gives the same instant directly, as lines 219-223 already do.
